title: Majestic Precision
reviewNotes: Reconstructed six-piece phase after ...h3 at 124 seconds. Three checked branches include checking before rook sacrifice, exact winning pawn blockade, actual stalemate after Rxg3 h2 and independent quiet a5, and losing Ke2 after ...Kxg3. Earlier seven-piece moves remain context.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius would be able to find the incredible win that white has in this position. You see, black is about to promote to a new queen with a check. And not only that, our only rook is hanging. So, we need to find a way to save the rook and stop the pawn promotion at the same time. But, it doesn't seem possible. If we move the rook behind the pawn, this seems to almost work. But, after G3 rook takes and H3, there is no way for us to stop G2 check and then G1 queen. White actually needs to be very careful to draw this. We can improve on that plan by starting with rook to G1 check, forcing king H2, rook G2 check, and then collecting the pawn. And now, we are in the same situation as before, but black did not get the opportunity to play G3. Now, black has two ways to try and proceed [music] in this position. Still play G3 or go for H3. If H3 is played, we have a very interesting idea. King to F2, opening up a check for the rook so that if H2 is played, this would simply be a checkmate. But, also we are stopping the pawn from going to G3. Of course, black has king to H2, but after rook to A1, we are taking away all of the legal moves that this king has apart from G3. [music] Up with the king, G2, and finally the nail in this coffin would be king to G4. Black only has one legal move to promote the pawn, but doing so would allow rook takes. The king has to take the rook, and then white would collect this pawn and promote this other pawn. So, going back to that crossroads of playing either H3 or G3, black is going to conclude that the better idea is to play G3 first. We cannot allow black to play H3 because otherwise, G2 is going to become unstoppable again. So, white has to play rook to g2 and prevent that idea. But, h3 not only is the only move that black can play, but it is also a clever trap. Because, if we do take the pawn, after pawn to h2, this pawn is blocked by the king and the king is blocked by both the rook and the king. We can only move away one at a time. So, this position would be a stalemate by force. So, white cannot collect this pawn and instead gives a check with the rook forcing king back to h2. Now, the pawn is defended by the king and if we take, we are both going to be left with a pawn and this would be a draw. Except, it wouldn't be. Because, all that matters is the placement of those pawns. The winning move is indeed rook takes g3. A brilliant sacrifice. Black takes, we can play king g1 and defend the promotion square. Black can push, but we're just going to step in front of the pawn and then we are going to be able to promote our pawn just in time to win the game.
